content.directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay that begins with the sentence "It is now widely accepted that mutual trust and openness is the key to promoting cooperation." You can make comments, cite examples or use your personal experiences to develop your essay. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.
content.topic: Mutual trust and openness as the key to promoting cooperation

modelEssay.title: Mutual Trust and Openness: The Key to Cooperation
modelEssay.content:
It is now widely accepted that mutual trust and openness is the key to promoting cooperation. In an era when individuals, organizations and even nations are deeply interconnected, no meaningful progress can be made if partners hide their true intentions or doubt one another's sincerity.

A telling example is the success of international scientific projects such as the Human Genome Project. Researchers from dozens of countries openly shared data, methods and even raw failures, which dramatically accelerated discoveries that no single laboratory could have achieved alone. In contrast, business partnerships built on suspicion often collapse the moment a small disagreement arises, since neither side is willing to give the other the benefit of the doubt.

In my own group projects at college, I have repeatedly observed that teams whose members speak frankly about both strengths and weaknesses outperform those who carefully guard their ideas. Therefore, cultivating trust and openness is not merely a moral virtue but a practical necessity if we hope to turn cooperation into shared success.

structureAnalysis.paragraph1: 引入段：照抄题目首句作为开篇，用 'In an era when... interconnected' 提升语境，反向论证缺乏信任与开放将阻碍合作
structureAnalysis.paragraph2: 展开段：双例对比 — 正例人类基因组计划展示开放共享加速科研; 反例多疑型商业合作易破裂, 形成正反对照
structureAnalysis.paragraph3: 总结段：以个人小组项目经历落到现实层面，最后将信任与开放从道德范畴提升到 'practical necessity', 收束有力

正反对比结构清晰 (Human Genome Project vs. suspicious partnerships)
高级表达: 'deeply interconnected' / 'give the benefit of the doubt' / 'practical necessity'
由宏观（国家/科研）→ 中观（商业）→ 微观（个人小组）三层论证, 层次分明

transcript.text: Welcome to Money Matters, a weekly program that helps you manage your money.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 欢迎收听《金钱事务》，这是一个帮助您管理资金的每周节目。

transcript.text: Tonight, I'll be talking to Mary Johnson about budgeting.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 今晚，我将与Mary Johnson讨论预算问题。

transcript.text: Hello, everyone.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 大家好。

transcript.text: There's a magic about money.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 金钱有一种魔力。

transcript.text: When it's not planned for, tracked, and kept a record of, it literally disappears.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 如果不对其计划、跟踪和记录，它真的会消失。

transcript.text: What are some of the steps we can take to prevent this from happening?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我们可以采取哪些步骤来防止这种情况发生？

transcript.text: Well, it's all about keeping track of your money.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 嗯，这完全在于跟踪您的资金。

transcript.text: If you don't do that, you'll never be able to set any goals for your budget or have the discipline to stick to them.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 如果您不这样做，您将永远无法为您的预算设定目标，或有纪律地坚持它们。

transcript.text: That's easier said than done.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 说起来容易做起来难。

transcript.text: I read recently that only 41% of Americans adhere to a budget.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我最近读到，只有41%的美国人遵守预算。

transcript.text: Yes, but knowing what you earn and what you spend can give you reassurance that you won't get into debt in the first place.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 是的，但了解您的收入和支出可以让您放心，您首先不会陷入债务。

transcript.text: You can do this by adding up all of your sources of income you have and writing them all down on a piece of paper.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 您可以通过将您所有的收入来源加总并写在一张纸上来做到这一点。

transcript.text: On the same page, write down all of your monthly expenses.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 在同一张纸上，写下您所有的月度开支。

transcript.text: I'm always amazed at how much my expenses add up, but designating each item as an income or an expense really helps me have a much better sense of all my spending.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我总是惊讶于我的开支加起来有多少，但将每个项目指定为收入或支出确实帮助我更好地了解我的所有支出。

transcript.text: Right.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 对。

transcript.text: Most people have no idea how much they spend each day, let alone each week or month, no matter how careful they are.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 大多数人不知道他们每天花多少钱，更不用说每周或每月了，无论他们多么小心。

transcript.text: Next, subtract your monthly expenses from income.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 接下来，从收入中减去您的月度开支。

transcript.text: If the result is positive, you are living within your means.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 如果结果是正数，您就是在量入为出。

transcript.text: If the result is a negative number, you're going to have to cut back on your spending.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 如果结果是负数，您将不得不削减开支。

transcript.text: I'm usually a negative number.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我通常是一个负数。

transcript.text: I just can't resist the allure of all those prestigious goods.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我就是无法抗拒那些名牌商品的诱惑。

transcript.text: Well, it's not a catastrophe, but you do have to make some changes.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 嗯，这不是灾难，但您确实需要做出一些改变。

transcript.text: Try cutting back on those non-essential items.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 试着减少那些非必需品。

transcript.text: Sell some stuff in your attic or shop online to avoid unnecessary temptations like chocolate.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 卖掉您阁楼里的一些东西，或者在网上购物以避免不必要的诱惑，比如巧克力。

transcript.text: Failing that, you can always find yourself a part-time job.

transcript.text: Passage 1.
transcript.translation: 文章1.

transcript.text: A new study has found a positive correlation between how much television children watch and their parents' stress levels.
transcript.translation: 一项新研究发现，儿童看电视的时间与父母压力水平之间存在正相关。

transcript.text: Why?
transcript.translation: 为什么？

transcript.text: Because the more television kids watch, the more they're exposed to advertising.
transcript.translation: 因为孩子们看电视越多，他们接触到的广告就越多。

transcript.text: The more advertising they see, the more likely they are to insist on purchasing items when they go with their parents to the store.
transcript.translation: 他们看到的广告越多，就越可能在和父母去商店时坚持购买物品。

transcript.text: This could generate conflict if the parents refuse.
transcript.translation: 如果父母拒绝，这可能会引发冲突。

transcript.text: All that, researchers say, can contribute to parents' overall stress levels.
transcript.translation: 研究人员说，所有这些都可能加剧父母的整体压力水平。

transcript.text: What's the solution?
transcript.translation: 解决方案是什么？

transcript.text: Perhaps the most obvious is curtailing screen time.
transcript.translation: 最明显的可能是减少屏幕时间。

transcript.text: Commercial content is there for a reason—to elicit purchasing behavior.
transcript.translation: 商业内容的存在是有原因的——为了引发购买行为。

transcript.text: So, parents might want to shut off the TV.
transcript.translation: 所以，父母可能想要关掉电视。

transcript.text: Researchers concede that this is easier said than done, so they suggest another option.
transcript.translation: 研究人员承认，这说起来容易做起来难，所以他们建议另一种选择。

transcript.text: Parents can change how they talk to their kids about purchases.
transcript.translation: 父母可以改变他们与孩子谈论购买的方式。

transcript.text: The researchers suggest that parents seek input from their children on family purchasing decisions.
transcript.translation: 研究人员建议父母在家庭购买决策中征求孩子的意见。

transcript.text: They shouldn't try to control all purchases.
transcript.translation: 他们不应该试图控制所有的购买。

transcript.text: Instead, parents might tell their children things like, I will listen to your advice on certain products or brands.
transcript.translation: 相反，父母可以对孩子说类似这样的话：我会听取你对某些产品或品牌的建议。

transcript.text: This type of communication, the researchers assert, can lead to children making fewer purchasing demands.
transcript.translation: 研究人员断言，这种沟通方式可以减少孩子提出的购买要求。

transcript.text: That means less parent stress.
transcript.translation: 这意味着父母压力更小。

transcript.text: However, the protective effect of this kind of communication diminishes with greater exposure to television.
transcript.translation: 然而，随着看电视时间的增加，这种沟通的保护作用会减弱。

transcript.text: This is because advertising aimed at children is especially persuasive.
transcript.translation: 这是因为针对儿童的广告特别具有说服力。

transcript.text: Advertisers use an assortment of tactics, such as bright colors, happy music, and celebrity endorsements, to appeal to children.
transcript.translation: 广告商使用各种策略，如明亮的颜色、快乐的音乐和名人代言，来吸引儿童。

transcript.text: Plus, children don't have the cognitive ability to fully understand advertising's intent.
transcript.translation: 此外，儿童没有认知能力来完全理解广告的意图。

transcript.text: That makes them particularly vulnerable to advertisements.
transcript.translation: 这使他们特别容易受到广告的影响。

transcript.translation: 每个人都应该为好人喝彩，我们只应惩罚坏人。

transcript.text: But that's not what we always do.
transcript.translation: 但我们并非总是这样做。

transcript.text: Most of the time, we do indeed reward good people.
transcript.translation: 大多数时候，我们确实会奖励好人。

transcript.text: We also often punish people who harm others or who aren't good team players.
transcript.translation: 我们也经常惩罚那些伤害他人或不善团队合作的人。

transcript.text: But sometimes, the good guys also get punished or criticized.
transcript.translation: 但有时，好人也会受到惩罚或批评。

transcript.text: Specifically, because they are so good.
transcript.translation: 具体来说，正是因为他们太好了。

transcript.text: This seems baffling, because it's detrimental to group cooperation.
transcript.translation: 这似乎令人困惑，因为它不利于群体合作。

transcript.text: However, the phenomenon has been discovered in multiple fields, and it has been found in every society.
transcript.translation: 然而，这一现象已在多个领域被发现，并且在每个社会中都存在。

transcript.text: Why does this happen?
transcript.translation: 为什么会这样？

transcript.text: Research suggests a simple reason.
transcript.translation: 研究指出了一个简单的原因。

transcript.text: When one person looks really good, others look bad by comparison.
transcript.translation: 当一个人看起来非常好时，相比之下，其他人就会显得不好。

transcript.text: Those others then have an incentive in stopping that person from looking good.
transcript.translation: 于是，那些人就有了阻止那个人表现出色的动力。

transcript.text: Especially if they can't or won't compete.
transcript.translation: 尤其是当他们不能或不愿竞争时。

transcript.text: After all, we're all judged in comparison with others.
transcript.translation: 毕竟，我们都是通过与他人比较来被评判的。

transcript.text: When faced with someone better, what can a normal person do?
transcript.translation: 当面对更优秀的人时，一个普通人能做什么？

transcript.text: One option is to actively compete.
transcript.translation: 一种选择是积极竞争。

transcript.text: A second option is to bring that person down.
transcript.translation: 第二种选择是贬低那个人。

transcript.text: That is, to suppress their cooperation or work ethic, infer selfish motives for their actions, or imply real or imagined hypocrisy.
transcript.translation: 也就是说，压制他们的合作精神或职业道德，推断他们行为的自私动机，或暗示真实或想象的虚伪。

transcript.text: Other tactics include attacking them on unrelated dimensions or punishing them outright.
transcript.translation: 其他策略包括在不相关的方面攻击他们，或直接惩罚他们。

transcript.text: Why does this matter?
transcript.translation: 为什么这很重要？

transcript.text: Critics often attack the motives of people who protect the environment, donate money, or work too hard.
transcript.translation: 批评者经常攻击那些保护环境、捐款或工作过于努力的人的动机。

transcript.text: Such good deeds are dismissed as naive or hypocritical by those who do not perform those deeds.
transcript.translation: 那些不做好事的人会将这些善行斥为天真或虚伪。

transcript.text: This criticism may ultimately discourage people from doing good deeds.
transcript.translation: 这种批评最终可能会阻止人们行善。

transcript.text: So it's important to recognize these attacks for what they are.
transcript.translation: 因此，认清这些攻击的本质很重要。

transcript.text: In America, most researchers concede that boys and girls are brought up in different ways, taught different skills, and rewarded for different acts.
transcript.translation: 在美国，大多数研究人员承认，男孩和女孩以不同的方式被抚养，学习不同的技能，并因不同的行为而受到奖励。

transcript.text: Women, it is agreed, excel at certain tasks, men at others.
transcript.translation: 人们普遍认为，女性擅长某些任务，男性则擅长其他任务。

transcript.text: There is little argument that some personality traits appear more dominant in one sex than in the other.
transcript.translation: 几乎没有争议的是，某些性格特征在一个性别中比另一个性别中更为突出。

transcript.text: All of this notwithstanding, gender differences are very much in the media these days.
transcript.translation: 尽管如此，如今媒体中性别差异的话题非常热门。

transcript.text: Since the rise of the women's movement, gender role behavior has come under closer scrutiny.
transcript.translation: 自妇女运动兴起以来，性别角色行为受到了更密切的审视。

transcript.text: How has this affected friendship?
transcript.translation: 这如何影响了友谊？

transcript.text: How do the sexes differ in their friendship relations?
transcript.translation: 两性在友谊关系上有何不同？

transcript.text: Most preteen children have a best friend who is usually someone of the same sex and similar age.
transcript.translation: 大多数青春期前的儿童有一个最好的朋友，通常是同性别且年龄相仿的人。

transcript.text: Both sexes share an essentially positive recollection of these childhood friendships.
transcript.translation: 两性对这些童年友谊的回忆基本上都是积极的。

transcript.text: They do not differ in this respect.
transcript.translation: 在这方面他们没有差异。

transcript.text: However, the type of play engaged in during these early friendships is telling of the difference to come.
transcript.translation: 然而，这些早期友谊中参与的游戏类型预示了未来的差异。

transcript.text: Boys tend to form playgroups that are competitive in nature.
transcript.translation: 男孩倾向于形成本质上具有竞争性的游戏小组。

transcript.text: Girls' groups more frequently revolve around cooperative enterprises.
transcript.translation: 女孩的小组更频繁地围绕合作性活动展开。

transcript.text: Thus, at an early age, boys become concerned with trying hard and winning, while girls, by contrast, play house and school, engaging in roles that require complementary support.
transcript.translation: 因此，在早期，男孩开始关注努力和胜利，而相比之下，女孩则玩过家家和上学游戏，参与需要互补支持的角色。

transcript.text: Speaking of their childhood, men recall being highly responsive to and aware of the gender role opinions of other boys.
transcript.translation: 谈到他们的童年，男性回忆起他们对其他男孩的性别角色意见高度敏感和意识。

transcript.text: Girls in preteen years appear to be less susceptible to gender role pressure.
transcript.translation: 青春期前的女孩似乎对性别角色压力不太敏感。

transcript.text: It is not until the dating years that women report being concerned with feminine behavior.
transcript.translation: 直到约会年龄，女性才报告她们关心女性化行为。

transcript.text: Males, for the most part, are responsive to the suggestion that their behavior is unmanly at almost any age.
transcript.translation: 男性，在大多数情况下，对他们的行为不够男子汉气概的暗示在几乎任何年龄都敏感。

transcript.text: These early attitudes, reinforced by social conditioning, continue to play an active part in the friendships of both sexes during adolescence.
transcript.translation: 这些早期态度，通过社会条件反射强化，继续在青春期两性的友谊中发挥积极作用。

transcript.text: This is a period when the majority of males once again report a close alliance with same-sex friends.
transcript.translation: 这是一个时期，大多数男性再次报告与同性朋友的紧密联盟。

transcript.text: Now, however, with heightened intensity, considerable energy is devoted to competing for position and a definite undercurrent of competition permeates the relationship.
transcript.translation: 然而，现在，随着强度增加，相当多的精力投入到争夺地位中，一种明确的竞争暗流渗透到关系中。

transcript.text: Although in dissimilar fashion, females share equally fragile relationships at this age.
transcript.translation: 尽管方式不同，女性在这个年龄同样拥有脆弱的关系。

transcript.text: For them, the bond of loyalty extends only to the line of romantic involvement.
transcript.translation: 对她们来说，忠诚的纽带仅延伸到恋爱关系的界限。

transcript.text: This is most apt to be the case in late adolescence, when dating and relationships with boys take sharp precedence over sisterhood.
transcript.translation: 这最可能发生在青春期晚期，当约会和与男孩的关系明显优先于姐妹情谊。

transcript.text: Actually, dating dilutes the intensity of same-sex friendships for men also.
transcript.translation: 实际上，约会也稀释了男性同性友谊的强度。

transcript.text: For the majority of us, the moment we begin to date seriously, there's a competition between romance and friendship.
transcript.translation: 对我们大多数人来说，当我们开始认真约会时，浪漫和友谊之间存在竞争。

transcript.text: Good afternoon!
transcript.translation: 下午好！

transcript.text: In today's lecture, we'll be talking about how and when to disclose a disability when applying for a job.
transcript.translation: 在今天的讲座中，我们将讨论在求职时如何以及何时披露残疾情况。

transcript.text: On average, about 20% of the population has some form of disability.
transcript.translation: 平均而言，大约20%的人口有某种形式的残疾。

transcript.text: Most countries these days have equal opportunity and non-discrimination laws.
transcript.translation: 如今，大多数国家都有机会平等和反歧视法律。

transcript.text: Yet, disabled people often find it hard to decide when, how, and if at all, to raise their disability problem with a potential employer.
transcript.translation: 然而，残疾人常常难以决定何时、如何，以及是否向潜在雇主提出他们的残疾问题。

transcript.text: There is uncertainty about how a recruiter will perceive their disability.
transcript.translation: 对于招聘人员如何看待他们的残疾，存在不确定性。

transcript.text: As such, many candidates fear they wouldn't be considered for a position as a result of disclosing this personal information.
transcript.translation: 因此，许多候选人担心由于披露这一个人信息，他们不会被考虑职位。

transcript.text: And research has validated this as a genuine concern for many job applicants.
transcript.translation: 而且研究证实，这是许多求职者的真正担忧。

transcript.text: It's a natural reaction, but it shouldn't be a reason to stay quiet.
transcript.translation: 这是一种自然反应，但不应成为保持沉默的理由。

transcript.text: People need to remember that they are applying for a position they have the skills and experience to excel in.
transcript.translation: 人们需要记住，他们申请的职位是他们拥有技能和经验能够胜任的。

transcript.text: Discussing a disability with a potential employer may help them make reasonable workplace adjustments in their favor.
transcript.translation: 与潜在雇主讨论残疾可能有助于他们做出有利于员工的合理工作场所调整。

transcript.text: It's most appropriate to discuss a disability when they reply to confirm an interview.
transcript.translation: 最合适的时候是在回复确认面试时讨论残疾。

transcript.text: This information needn't be put up front in their cover letter or resume because it's probably not relevant to the position itself.
transcript.translation: 这些信息不需要在求职信或简历中前置，因为它可能与职位本身无关。

transcript.text: Candidates with disabilities should feel they have the power to make their own decisions around sharing this information free from prejudice.
transcript.translation: 残疾候选人应感到自己有权力在分享此信息时不受偏见地做出自己的决定。

transcript.text: If they find an organization that doesn't celebrate diversity and inclusion, it could say a lot about the company's culture.
transcript.translation: 如果他们发现一个不倡导多样性和包容性的组织，这可能说明该公司的文化。

transcript.text: Perhaps the organization isn't the right fit.
transcript.translation: 或许这个组织并不合适。

transcript.text: It's important for them to remember that they are seeking a manager and employer that's going to be supportive and continue to give them a great employment experience.
transcript.translation: 重要的是，他们要记住，他们正在寻找一个支持性并继续提供良好就业体验的经理和雇主。

transcript.text: Companies sometimes offer candidates the chance to disclose disabilities on their application form.
transcript.translation: 公司有时会为候选人在申请表上提供披露残疾的机会。

transcript.text: But people shouldn't feel restricted by this method or timing.
transcript.translation: 但人们不应受限于这种方法或时机。

transcript.text: People should avoid sharing the name of their disability or condition.
transcript.translation: 人们应避免分享其残疾或病症的名称。

transcript.text: There is always the risk that the recruiter will research information that is inaccurate or irrelevant.
transcript.translation: 总是存在风险，即招聘人员研究的信息不准确或不相关。

transcript.text: If people don't think their disability will impact their ability to perform in the advertised position, then it's entirely their entitlement to choose when and whether to share this information.
transcript.translation: 如果人们认为他们的残疾不会影响他们在所广告职位上的表现，那么他们完全有权选择何时以及是否分享此信息。

transcript.text: Recording 3.
transcript.translation: 录音3。

transcript.text: Smartphones distract attention and reduce learning because of their potential to offer activities more inviting than study.
transcript.translation: 智能手机分散注意力并减少学习，因为它们可能提供比学习更具吸引力的活动。

transcript.text: But what about background sound alone?
transcript.translation: 但单独的背景声音呢？

transcript.text: A group of American researchers compared students' comprehension of verbal material when reading in the presence of background speech, instrumental music, or general noise.
transcript.translation: 一组美国研究人员比较了学生在背景言语、器乐或一般噪音存在下阅读时对文字材料的理解。

transcript.text: General noise is neutral, such as that from the sound of an air conditioner or fan.
transcript.translation: 一般噪音是中性的，例如来自空调或风扇的声音。

transcript.text: Students' scores were most depressed in the presence of background speech.
transcript.translation: 在背景言语存在下，学生的分数最低。

transcript.text: Comprehension was slightly better with the presence of music than with speech.
transcript.translation: 有音乐存在时，理解力比有言语时稍好。

transcript.text: However, when they were asked to identify melodies rather than understand text, background music interfered more.
transcript.translation: 然而，当他们被要求识别旋律而不是理解文本时，背景音乐的干扰更大。

transcript.text: When the background speech was in a language unfamiliar to participants, there was little, if any, hindrance of reading comprehension.
transcript.translation: 当背景言语使用参与者不熟悉的语言时，对阅读理解几乎没有阻碍。

transcript.text: British researchers compared the effects of background speech, vocal music, instrumental music, general background noise, and silence on short-term memory.
transcript.translation: 英国研究人员比较了背景言语、声乐、器乐、一般背景噪音和寂静对短期记忆的影响。

transcript.text: Background speech had the biggest negative effect.
transcript.translation: 背景言语的负面影响最大。

transcript.text: Vocal music was slightly more disruptive than instrumental.
transcript.translation: 声乐比器乐更具干扰性。

transcript.text: In general, background noise and silence were least disruptive.
transcript.translation: 总体而言，背景噪音和寂静的干扰最小。

transcript.text: It seems the degree of interference from background noise depends on the overlap between the processing required on the task and the processing required to screen out the background noise.
transcript.translation: 似乎背景噪音的干扰程度取决于任务所需的处理与屏蔽背景噪音所需的处理之间的重叠。

transcript.text: The studies suggest that when people read and when they try to remember any verbal material, background speech will inhibit their ability.
transcript.translation: 研究表明，当人们阅读或尝试记住任何文字材料时，背景言语会抑制他们的能力。

transcript.text: Instrumental music will have, at worst, a slight effect.
transcript.translation: 器乐最多只会产生轻微影响。

transcript.text: When students write essays, however, other research has found it is best to reduce all background noise as much as possible.
transcript.translation: 然而，当学生写作文时，其他研究发现最好尽可能减少所有背景噪音。

transcript.text: Not everyone reacts in the same way to distractions.
transcript.translation: 并非所有人对干扰的反应都相同。

transcript.text: Other studies suggest some aspects of personality may make a difference.
transcript.translation: 其他研究表明，性格的某些方面可能会产生影响。

transcript.text: The researchers subjected shy, quiet people and confident, outgoing ones to high-arousal or low-arousal background music, general noise, or silence while asking them to remember words.

paragraphs.text: The now extinct passenger pigeon has the dubious honor of being the last species anyone ever expected to disappear. At one point, there were more passenger pigeons than any other species of bird. Rough __26__ of their population went as high as five billion and they accounted for around 40 percent of the total indigenous bird population of North America in the early 19th century.
paragraphs.translation: 现已灭绝的旅鸽拥有一种不光彩的殊荣，即它是人们最不期望消失的物种。曾经，旅鸽的数量超过任何其他鸟类。粗略估计其种群数量高达五十亿，在19世纪初，约占北美本地鸟类总数的40%。

paragraphs.text: Despite their huge population, passenger pigeons were __27__ to human intrusion into their nesting territory. Their nests were shabby things and two weeks after the eggs __28__, the parent pigeons would abandon their offspring, leaving them to take care of themselves. People discovered that these baby pigeons were really tasty, and the adult birds were also quite __29__. First the Native Americans and then the transplanted Europeans came to consider the birds a great __30__.
paragraphs.translation: 尽管种群庞大，旅鸽却容易受到人类侵入其筑巢领地的威胁。它们的巢穴简陋，在卵孵化两周后，亲鸽会抛弃幼鸟，让它们自谋生路。人们发现这些幼鸽非常美味，成年鸟类也相当可食。先是美洲原住民，后来是移居的欧洲人，都视这种鸟为美味佳肴。

paragraphs.text: By the 1850s, commercial trapping of passenger pigeons was proceeding at an __31__ pace. Hundreds of thousands of the birds were being harvested every day to be made into popular pigeon pies. In addition, large __32__ of the pigeons' nesting territory were being cleared away for planting crops and creating pasture land. As numerous as the passenger pigeons were, they were not an __33__ resource. By the 1880s, it was noticed that the bird population had become seriously __34__. The last passenger pigeons killed in the wild were shot in 1899.
paragraphs.translation: 到了19世纪50年代，旅鸽的商业捕猎正以空前的速度进行。每天有数十万只鸟被捕获，制成受欢迎的鸽肉馅饼。此外，大片旅鸽的筑巢领地被清除，用于种植作物和开辟牧场。尽管旅鸽数量众多，但并非无限资源。到19世纪80年代，人们注意到鸟群数量已严重枯竭。最后在野外被杀的旅鸽是在1899年被射杀的。

paragraphs.text: Eventually those billions and billions of birds shrank to a single remaining __35__, a passenger pigeon named Martha, who died on September 1, 1914, in captivity at the Cincinnati Zoo. In addition to being the end of an era, it was also the first time humans were able to exactly time the extinction of a species.
paragraphs.translation: 最终，那数十亿只鸟缩减到仅剩一个标本，一只名为玛莎的旅鸽，于1914年9月1日在辛辛那提动物园的囚禁中死亡。这不仅是一个时代的终结，也是人类首次能够准确记录一个物种的灭绝时间。

questionGroups.title: Is computer coding a foreign language?

material.title: Is computer coding a foreign language?

paragraphs.text: As computer coding has become an increasingly sought-after skill, more K-12 schools are working it into their curriculums. Some states have considered allowing students to forgo (放弃) foreign language for coding classes, despite opposition from educators.
paragraphs.translation: 随着计算机编程成为日益抢手的技能，越来越多的K-12学校正将其纳入课程。尽管有教育工作者的反对，一些州已考虑允许学生放弃外语课程以选修编程课。

paragraphs.text: There's a debate over whether it's appropriate to teach coding in elementary schools, with fierce opinions on each side. When it comes to allowing coding to fill foreign language requirements, though, most educators agree: Coding should be added to curriculums, but not at the expense of foreign language classes.
paragraphs.translation: 关于在小学教授编程是否合适存在争议，双方观点激烈。然而，当涉及允许编程课程满足外语要求时，大多数教育工作者一致认为：编程应加入课程，但不应以牺牲外语课为代价。

paragraphs.text: The idea is that computer programming is a language, allowing people to communicate with machines and programs. It's the language of the 21st century and more valuable than a natural language, some advocates argue. The computer science field is growing faster than schools can keep up because of budget constraints and a lack of skills training for teachers.
paragraphs.translation: 这种观点认为计算机编程是一种语言，允许人们与机器和程序交流。一些倡导者认为，它是21世纪的语言，比自然语言更有价值。由于预算限制和教师技能培训的缺乏，计算机科学领域的发展速度超过了学校的跟进能力。

paragraphs.text: According to the 2016 U.S. News/Raytheon STEM Index, computer science jobs have helped boost wages in the U.S., and computer-related jobs hold the top seven positions in STEM fields for the highest number of workers. Foreign language interest, on the other hand, is declining for the first time since 1995. The number of higher education language enrollments declined between 2009 and 2013 by more than 111,000 spots, according to the Modern Language Association of America.
paragraphs.translation: 根据2016年美国新闻/雷神公司STEM指数，计算机科学工作帮助提升了美国的工资水平，计算机相关工作在STEM领域中工人数量排名前七。另一方面，外语兴趣自1995年以来首次下降。根据美国现代语言协会的数据，2009年至2013年间，高等教育语言入学人数减少了超过111,000个名额。

paragraphs.text: "I think the opportunity to give people a choice is important," says Florida state Senator Jeremy Ring, who introduced a bill last year that would allow Florida students to choose between foreign language and coding classes for the purpose of university admissions requirements. "I think if you're going to give two years of language in high school, you might as well do computer coding."
paragraphs.translation: “我认为给人选择的机会很重要，”佛罗里达州参议员杰里米·林说，他去年提出了一项法案，允许佛罗里达学生在外语课和编程课之间选择，以满足大学入学要求。“我认为如果你在高中要上两年语言课，不如学计算机编程。”

paragraphs.text: The Florida bill died this year after passing 35:5 in the state Senate when the full Legislature failed to take action. It would have been the first state to try this initiative. Ring says that although he will be out of office, an identical bill will be reintroduced within the next year by others on his behalf. "In the speech I gave on the Senate floor, I said, 'We can be the first state to do this, or we can be the 50th state to do it. It's our choice. It's going to happen,'" Ring says.
paragraphs.translation: 佛罗里达州法案在州参议院以35:5通过后，因州议会未能采取行动而今年夭折。该州本可能成为第一个尝试这一举措的州。林表示，尽管他将离任，但明年将有他人代表他重新提出相同的法案。“我在参议院的演讲中说过，‘我们可以成为第一个这样做的州，也可以成为第五十个这样做的州。这是我们的选择。它将会发生，’”林说。

paragraphs.text: A Kentucky bill similar to the one in Florida was met with complaints from educators, and was then amended to promote computer science education initiatives with no mention of foreign language requirements. Instead, the state will provide support for higher quality certified teachers for programming classes. Under the Washington bill, public universities would accept two years of computer science classes in place of two years of foreign language for admission purposes. A report detailing the opinions of state university officials is due to the Legislature by November 2017.
paragraphs.translation: 肯塔基州一项类似佛罗里达州的法案遭到教育工作者的投诉，随后被修订以促进计算机科学教育举措，未提及外语要求。相反，该州将为编程课提供更高质量的认证教师支持。根据华盛顿州法案，公立大学将接受两年的计算机科学课程代替两年的外语课程作为入学要求。一份详细说明州大学官员意见的报告将于2017年11月提交给州议会。

paragraphs.text: Texas passed a bill in 2013 that allows students to substitute computer coding only after they have attempted and performed poorly in a foreign language class. Srini Mandyam, CTO and co-founder of kid-friendly instructional coding company Tynker, believes allowing students to forgo foreign language because they struggle with it is unproductive because every subject, whether art, math or language, is a significant contribution to a well-rounded existence. "Many students don't fare well with algebra but we never discuss eliminating it or … say chemistry is now counted as an algebra class," he said via email. "We teach algebra because it's important and we should teach foreign languages and coding for the same reason. Exposure to a wide breadth of subjects and material results in well-rounded students who are able to make informed decisions … about what they want to pursue."
paragraphs.translation: 德克萨斯州在2013年通过了一项法案，允许学生在尝试外语课并表现不佳后才能用计算机编程替代。Srini Mandyam，儿童友好型编程教学公司Tynker的首席技术官兼联合创始人，认为允许学生因为学习困难而放弃外语是低效的，因为每个学科，无论是艺术、数学还是语言，都对全面发展的生活有重要贡献。“许多学生代数成绩不好，但我们从未讨论取消它或……说化学现在算作代数课，”他通过电子邮件说。“我们教代数是因为它重要，我们应该以同样的理由教外语和编程。接触广泛的学科和材料能培养全面发展的学生，他们能够就自己想要追求的目标做出明智的决定。”

paragraphs.text: Computer science courses already fulfill a math or science high school graduation requirement in 28 states and the District of Columbia, up from only 12 states in 2013. And while advocates of the bills say they should count as foreign language instead, opponents stress the importance of balancing computer and foreign language skills.
paragraphs.translation: 计算机科学课程已在28个州和哥伦比亚特区满足高中毕业的数学或科学要求，而2013年仅有12个州。尽管法案倡导者认为它们应算作外语课程，但反对者强调平衡计算机和外语技能的重要性。

paragraphs.text: Studies show that bilingualism (双语) correlates with cognitive development, intelligence, memory and problem solving abilities, according to the American Council on the Teaching of Foreign Languages. A 2007 study showed that foreign language students outperformed their non-foreign language peers on standardized tests after only two to three years of study. And while a 2014 report from German and American universities suggests that programmers are using language (but not mathematical) regions of the brain when understanding code, critics remain wary. They say that regardless of cognitive functions, being monolingual is a disadvantage in the increasingly international economy, even if English has become the de facto (事实上的) language of business.
paragraphs.translation: 根据美国外语教学委员会的研究，双语能力与认知发展、智力、记忆和问题解决能力相关。2007年的一项研究表明，仅经过两到三年学习，外语学生在标准化测试中表现优于非外语同龄人。尽管德国和美国大学2014年的一份报告表明，程序员在理解代码时使用大脑的语言（而非数学）区域，但批评者仍持谨慎态度。他们表示，无论认知功能如何，在日益国际化的经济中，单语是一种劣势，即使英语已成为事实上的商业语言。

paragraphs.text: "Our world is shrinking but its problems are really growing," says ACTFL National Language Teacher of the Year Ted Zarrow, who teaches high school Latin in Westwood, Massachusetts, and has also studied Spanish, French, German, Italian and Greek. "We need to find a way to put ourselves at the global table and to treat each other with mutual respect. And learning languages allows us to do that because language is not part of culture, language is culture."
paragraphs.translation: “我们的世界在缩小，但问题确实在增加，”美国外语教学委员会年度国家语言教师泰德·扎罗说，他在马萨诸塞州韦斯特伍德教授高中拉丁语，还学习过西班牙语、法语、德语、意大利语和希腊语。“我们需要找到一种方式，让自己坐在全球谈判桌前，并以相互尊重的方式对待彼此。学习语言让我们能做到这一点，因为语言不是文化的一部分，语言就是文化。”

paragraphs.text: Even with the benefits and skill sets languages provide, recruiters and employers value computer skills more. According to the National Association of Colleges and Employers' 2016 report, study abroad and foreign language fluency were not very influential in the employee hiring processes, but 55 percent of employers looked for computer skills on applicants' resumes. However, although 2016 computer science graduates can expect to make the second highest starting salary compared with other jobs this year, the Bureau of Labor predicts the demand for computer programmers will decrease 8 percent or by 26,500 jobs by 2024.
paragraphs.translation: 尽管语言提供了好处和技能组合，但招聘人员和雇主更重视计算机技能。根据美国大学与雇主协会2016年的报告，留学和外语流利度在招聘过程中影响不大，但55%的雇主在求职者简历中寻找计算机技能。然而，尽管2016年计算机科学毕业生今年与其他工作相比有望获得第二高的起薪，但劳工局预测，到2024年，对计算机程序员的需求将下降8%或减少26,500个工作岗位。

paragraphs.text: Ring says foreign language skills are important, but expresses doubt that school districts could work both coding and language into their curriculum in a significant way because they lack the time in the school day. "Nothing against language," he says. "I just think it's something you have to start early and not just have something that you do for a couple years in high school," he says.
paragraphs.translation: 林表示外语技能重要，但怀疑学区能否以重要方式将编程和语言都纳入课程，因为学校日时间不足。“并非反对语言，”他说。“我只是认为这是你必须早点开始的事情，而不是仅仅在高中做几年，”他说。

paragraphs.text: Zarrow agrees that foreign language education should begin earlier, but says it is possible to work both computer programming and foreign language learning into schools evenly. He suggests an immersive, dual language program where students spend half the day in English and half the day in another language, as several schools around the country have successfully implemented. "The study of language fosters a respect for diversity, a respect for ethnicity and really a respect for language," Zarrow says.
paragraphs.translation: 扎罗同意外语教育应更早开始，但表示有可能在学校均衡地安排计算机编程和外语学习。他建议采用沉浸式双语项目，学生半天用英语学习，半天用另一语言学习，正如全国几所学校已成功实施的那样。“语言学习培养对多样性、对种族以及对语言的尊重，”扎罗说。

paragraphs.text: Though the benefits of computer programming skills are vast, foreign language and coding experts agree that computer science should be negotiated into curriculums rather than replacing foreign language outright. Mandyam says the two skill sets are essential but unrelated. "Coding is an incredibly important 21st century skill for our kids to learn, and that's why we spend so much time trying to teach it," Mandyam says via email. "But I believe it is the same as or even really comparable to learning a foreign language. It would be a shame to lose something so important for the sake of adding something else, even something as important as coding. Clearly, education leaders must figure out a way to teach both."
paragraphs.translation: 尽管计算机编程技能的好处广泛，但外语和编程专家一致认为，计算机科学应协商纳入课程，而不是完全取代外语。Mandyam说这两种技能组合都重要但不相关。“编程是我们的孩子学习的重要21世纪技能，这就是我们花这么多时间试图教授它的原因，”Mandyam通过电子邮件说。“但我认为它与学习外语相同甚至真的相当。为了添加其他东西而失去如此重要的东西将是遗憾，即使像编程这样重要的东西。显然，教育领导者必须找到一种方式来教授两者。

questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落L。段落L中提到'According to the National Association of Colleges and Employers' 2016 report, study abroad and foreign language fluency were not very influential in the employee hiring processes, but 55 percent of employers looked for computer skills on applicants' resumes.' 这表明雇主在招聘过程中更看重申请者的计算机技能而非语言能力。

questions.statementText: One U.S. state senator proposed that high school students be allowed to study either foreign language or computer coding.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落E。段落E中提到'Florida state Senator Jeremy Ring, who introduced a bill last year that would allow Florida students to choose between foreign language and coding classes for the purpose of university admissions requirements.' 这表明一位美国州参议员提议允许高中生学习外语或计算机编程。

questions.statementText: Learning languages broadens students' international perspective and nurtures mutual respect among peoples, according to a high school language teacher.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落K。段落K中提到'learning languages allows us to do that because language is not part of culture, language is culture.' 这表明学习语言可以拓宽学生的国际视野并培养各国人民之间的相互尊重。

questions.statementText: One U.S. state will see to it that programming classes are taught by quality teachers.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落G。段落G中提到'the state will provide support for higher quality certified teachers for programming classes.' 这表明一个美国州将确保编程课程由高质量的教师教授。

questions.statementText: Statistics show while computer-related jobs have been on the rise, foreign languages have become less appealing to American students since mid-1990s.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落D。段落D中提到'Foreign language interest, on the other hand, is declining for the first time since 1995.' 这表明自1995年中期以来，外语对美国学生吸引力下降，而计算机相关工作数量在上升。

questions.statementText: All school subjects are said to be essential to students' well-rounded development.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落H。段落H中提到'every subject, whether art, math or language, is a significant contribution to a well-rounded existence.' 这表明所有学校科目都被认为是对学生全面发展至关重要的。

questions.statementText: There is consensus among most educators that coding should be taught in schools but should not replace foreign language.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落B。段落B中提到'most educators agree: Coding should be added to curriculums, but not at the expense of foreign language classes.' 这表明大多数教育工作者达成共识，认为应该在学校教授编程，但不应取代外语课。

questions.statementText: One study showed that foreign language learning improved students' academic performance.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落J。段落J中提到'A 2007 study showed that foreign language students outperformed their non-foreign language peers on standardized tests after only two to three years of study.' 这表明一项研究表明外语学习提高了学生的学术表现。

questions.statementText: Being short of funding and qualified teachers, schools lag behind the fast developing computer science field.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落C。段落C中提到'The computer science field is growing faster than schools can keep up because of budget constraints and a lack of skills training for teachers.' 这表明由于资金和合格教师的缺乏，学校跟不上快速发展的计算机科学领域。

questions.statementText: A distinguished high school language teacher also believes it is advisable to start learning a foreign language at an earlier age.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落N。段落N中提到'Zarrow agrees that foreign language education should begin earlier,' 这表明这位杰出的高中语言教师也认为应该更早开始学习外语。

questionGroups.title: Passage One

paragraphs.text: The U.S. and China don't agree on much these days. Germany and France share a border and a currency but are frequently at odds. The U.K. and India like to march to their own drum. But there's one issue on which all these countries see eye to eye: Technology companies are too big, too powerful, and too profitable. And that power is only likely to intensify, leaving governments with no choice but to confront it head-on by taking the companies to court, passing new competition laws, and perhaps even breaking up the tech giants.
paragraphs.translation: 近年来，美国和中国在许多问题上存在分歧。德国和法国共享边界和货币，但经常意见不一。英国和印度喜欢特立独行。但有一个问题，所有这些国家都意见一致：科技公司过于庞大、过于强大、过于盈利。而且这种权力只会加剧，使得政府别无选择，只能通过将公司告上法庭、通过新的竞争法，甚至可能拆分科技巨头来直面应对。

paragraphs.text: China is the latest to implement an anti-trust crackdown, unveiling anti-monopoly rules last month. The draft rules followed the surprise suspension of a $37 billion stock offering by billionaire Jack Ma's Ant Group Co., making clear that no company can evade the government's regulation. The moves in China coincide with accelerating efforts in the U.S. and Europe to rein in Amazon.com, Apple, Facebook, and Google.
paragraphs.translation: 中国是最新实施反垄断打击的国家，上月公布了反垄断规则。这些规则草案紧随亿万富翁马云的蚂蚁集团意外暂停370亿美元股票发行之后，明确表示任何公司都无法逃避政府监管。中国的这些举措与美国和欧洲加快约束亚马逊、苹果、Facebook和谷歌的努力同步进行。

paragraphs.text: "The big get bigger and bigger but without being better," says Andreas Schwab, a German member of the European Parliament who championed a 2014 resolution to break up Google. "Growing economic power, growing influence on local markets all over the world, and a growing concern of competitors and consumers altogether have made it happen now."
paragraphs.translation: “企业变得越来越大，但并未变得更好，”欧洲议会议员Andreas Schwab说，他曾倡导2014年一项拆分谷歌的决议。“不断增长的经济实力、对全球各地市场日益增长的影响力，以及竞争对手和消费者日益增长的担忧，共同促成了现在的局面。”

paragraphs.text: In this new anti-trust era, the old focus on pricing power no longer applies, because several of the biggest tech companies have established trillion-dollar monopolies by charging consumers next to nothing. Tech giants are increasingly assuming powerful positions in banking, finance, advertising, retail, and other markets that force smaller businesses to rely on their platforms to reach customers.
paragraphs.translation: 在这个新的反垄断时代，旧的对定价权的关注不再适用，因为几家最大的科技公司通过向消费者收取几乎为零的费用，建立了万亿美元的垄断地位。科技巨头在银行、金融、广告、零售和其他市场中日益占据强大地位，迫使小企业依赖它们的平台来接触客户。

paragraphs.text: For years, Europe alone confronted the power of digital giants. Governments were alarmed that European companies were failing to match Silicon Valley's innovations or to stop Google and Facebook from vacuuming up personal data and, with that, advertising revenue. Led by Margrethe Vestager, the European Union's competition chief, countries have sought to police the market and encourage fair play.
paragraphs.translation: 多年来，欧洲独自面对数字巨头的权力。政府震惊于欧洲公司未能匹敌硅谷的创新，或阻止谷歌和Facebook吸走个人数据及其带来的广告收入。在欧盟竞争事务专员Margrethe Vestager的领导下，各国试图监管市场并鼓励公平竞争。

paragraphs.text: In China the crackdown has been driven at least partly by fear that the homegrown tech industry is becoming too powerful. The country has long championed Alibaba and Tencent, but their massive accumulation of data on the Chinese citizenry is a growing concern for Beijing.
paragraphs.translation: 在中国，反垄断打击至少部分是由对本土科技行业变得过于强大的担忧所驱动。该国长期以来支持阿里巴巴和腾讯，但它们对中国公民数据的大规模积累日益引起北京的担忧。

paragraphs.text: In the U.S., a new breed of anti-trust experts argues that consideration should be given to privacy, control over data, workers' rights, and the overall impact on smaller companies. And the public in general have grown increasingly skeptical of social media companies. More than 60% say the sector has a negative effect on the country, and almost half want more regulation for social media, according to a 2020 Pew Research Center study.
paragraphs.translation: 在美国，新一代反垄断专家认为，应考虑隐私、数据控制、工人权益以及对小企业的整体影响。公众总体上对社交媒体公司越来越怀疑。根据2020年皮尤研究中心的一项研究，超过60%的人表示该行业对国家有负面影响，近半数人希望对社交媒体进行更多监管。

questionGroups.directions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.questionText: What does the author say is the issue all major economic powers have to address?

options.label: A
options.text: How to ensure the sustainable growth of their tech giants.

options.label: B
options.text: How to keep the competitiveness of their tech companies.

options.label: C
options.text: How to break up the powerful giant tech companies.

options.label: D
options.text: How to stop tech companies from gaining monopoly.

questions.analysis: 这是一道主旨大意题。文章第一段提到各国都认为科技公司太大、太强、太有利可图，并且这种力量只会加剧，迫使政府必须直面这个问题。因此D选项是正确答案

wrongOptions.A: 'How to ensure the sustainable growth of their tech giants'与文章主旨不符，文章讨论的是科技公司的负面影响
wrongOptions.B: 'How to keep the competitiveness of their tech companies'只是问题的一方面，不是主旨
wrongOptions.C: 'How to break up the powerful giant tech companies'是解决措施之一，但不是文章讨论的核心问题

questions.questionText: What does the suspension of Ant Group Co.'s stock offering suggest?

options.label: A
options.text: All attempts to evade regulation are doomed to failure.

options.label: B
options.text: All attempts to monopolize sales must be cracked down.

options.label: C
options.text: All companies must be regulated by the government.

options.label: D
options.text: All companies, domestic or foreign, are created equal.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。文章提到中国实施反垄断打击，暂停了蚂蚁集团370亿美元的上市计划，表明没有公司可以逃避政府的监管。因此C选项是正确答案

wrongOptions.A: 'All attempts to evade regulation are doomed to failure'过于绝对，文章没有提到所有逃避监管的尝试都会失败
wrongOptions.B: 'All attempts to monopolize sales must be cracked down'只是反垄断打击的一个方面，不是文章讨论的重点
wrongOptions.D: 'All companies, domestic or foreign, are created equal'与文章内容无关

questions.questionText: How are smaller companies impacted by tech giants' business expansion?

options.label: A
options.text: They can no longer do business independent of tech giants.

options.label: B
options.text: They are frequently denied access to tech giants' platforms.

options.label: C
options.text: They have to change marketing strategies to keep customers.

options.label: D
options.text: They no longer have the power to price their own products.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。文章提到科技巨头在多个市场占据越来越重要的位置，迫使小企业依赖他们的平台来接触客户。因此A选项是正确答案

wrongOptions.B: 'They are frequently denied access to tech giants' platforms'与文章内容不符，文章没有提到小企业被拒绝使用科技巨头的平台
wrongOptions.C: 'They have to change marketing strategies to keep customers'只是小企业受影响的一个方面，不是主要影响
wrongOptions.D: 'They no longer have the power to price their own products'与文章内容不符，文章没有提到小企业失去定价权

questions.questionText: What have EU countries done to confront the power of digital giants?

options.label: A
options.text: They have imposed strict regulation over digital giants' advertising.

options.label: B
options.text: They have considered regulatory action to promote fair competition.

options.label: C
options.text: They have limited sales of digital giants' products.

options.label: D
options.text: They have sought to protect consumers' privacy.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。文章提到在欧洲，以维斯塔格为首的欧盟竞争事务主管领导各国寻求监管市场，鼓励公平竞争。因此B选项是正确答案

wrongOptions.A: 'They have imposed strict regulation over digital giants' advertising'与文章内容不符，文章没有提到对数字巨头的广告进行严格监管
wrongOptions.C: 'They have limited sales of digital giants' products'与文章内容不符，文章没有提到限制数字巨头的产品销售
wrongOptions.D: 'They have sought to protect consumers' privacy'只是欧盟采取的措施之一，不是主要措施

questions.questionText: What do Americans generally think of social media companies according to the author?

options.label: A
options.text: They are invading people's privacy.

options.label: B
options.text: They are increasingly influential.

options.label: C
options.text: They are becoming untrustworthy.

options.label: D
options.text: They are growing out of control.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。题干问美国公众对社交媒体公司的总体看法。原文 'the public in general have grown increasingly skeptical of social media companies' 是关键句，skeptical（怀疑、不信任）直接对应 C 选项 'They are becoming untrustworthy（变得不可信）'；后文 'More than 60% say the sector has a negative effect' 进一步印证这种不信任态度。语法/逻辑上，skeptical of 后接对象表明信任度下降，故选 C。

wrongOptions.A: 'They are invading people's privacy' 只是反垄断专家提到的考量之一，并非公众对社交媒体公司的总体态度
wrongOptions.B: 'They are increasingly influential' 原文未提及公众认为其影响力在增加，与 skeptical 的语义不符
wrongOptions.D: 'They are growing out of control' 原文没有 out of control（失控）的表述，属无中生有

questionGroups.title: Passage Two

paragraphs.text: Born from the accessibility of mass air travel, modern international tourism has been popularized as "holiday-making" in regions that offer comparative advantages of sand, sun and sea. Travel is often portrayed as a tool for personal growth and tourism as an economic motor for destination countries and cities. There is a tendency to assume that tourism is good for everyone involved.
paragraphs.translation: 现代国际旅游源于大众航空旅行的便利性，在拥有沙、阳光和海洋比较优势的地区，已被普及为“度假”。旅行常被描绘为个人成长的工具，而旅游则是目的地国家和城市的经济引擎。人们倾向于认为旅游对所有相关方都有益。

paragraphs.text: Today the big bang of tourism drives over 1.2 billion tourists across international borders annually. Many popular places are literally being loved to death. Recent protests in ports of call like Venice and Barcelona against disturbances created by cruise ships show the unfortunate consequences of emphasizing quantity over quality in tourism.
paragraphs.translation: 如今，旅游业的迅猛发展每年推动超过12亿游客跨越国际边界。许多热门地点简直被过度喜爱而濒临毁灭。最近在威尼斯和巴塞罗那等停靠港口，针对邮轮造成干扰的抗议活动显示了在旅游业中强调数量而非质量的不幸后果。

paragraphs.text: Uncontrolled tourism development has become a primary driver of social and environmental disruption. Tourism studies provide much documentation of the many negative social impacts of tourism and resulting resentment that local populations direct toward visitors.
paragraphs.translation: 不受控制的旅游发展已成为社会和环境破坏的主要驱动力。旅游研究提供了大量关于旅游许多负面社会影响的文献，以及由此导致的当地居民对游客的怨恨。

paragraphs.text: Antagonism toward tourists typically develops in mature, heavily visited destinations. Protests in heavily visited destinations suggest that traditional tourism has overstayed its welcome.
paragraphs.translation: 对游客的敌意通常出现在成熟、游客密集的目的地。在游客密集目的地的抗议表明，传统旅游已经不受欢迎。

paragraphs.text: Residents often become frustrated when the benefits of tourism are not felt locally. Although it can generate foreign exchange, income and employment, there's no guarantee that multinational hotel chains will allocate these benefits equitably among local communities.
paragraphs.translation: 当旅游的好处在当地未被感受到时，居民常常感到沮丧。尽管旅游能带来外汇、收入和就业，但无法保证跨国酒店连锁店会将这些利益公平分配给当地社区。

paragraphs.text: On the contrary, when people stay at large resorts or on cruise ships, they make most of their purchases there, leaving local communities little opportunity to benefit from tourist spending. These forms of tourism widen economic and political gaps between haves and have-nots at local destinations.
paragraphs.translation: 相反，当人们住在大型度假村或邮轮上时，他们大部分购物都在那里进行，使当地社区很少有机会从游客消费中受益。这些旅游形式扩大了当地目的地富人和穷人之间的经济和政治差距。

paragraphs.text: In recent decades, local residents in destination communities also have found themselves negotiating new cultural boundaries, class dynamics, service industry roles and lifestyle transformations. For example, data show that tourism activity corresponds to increased social problems as local residents adopt the behaviors of tourists.
paragraphs.translation: 近几十年来，目的地社区的当地居民也发现自己在应对新的文化界限、阶级动态、服务业角色和生活方式转变。例如，数据显示，旅游活动与当地居民模仿游客行为导致的社会问题增加相对应。

paragraphs.text: What does all this mean for the everyday traveler?
paragraphs.translation: 所有这些对普通旅行者意味着什么？

paragraphs.text: First, all tourists should make every effort to honor their hosts and respect local conditions. This means being prepared to adapt to local customs and norms, rather than expecting local conditions to adapt to travelers.
paragraphs.translation: 首先，所有游客应尽力尊重东道主和当地环境。这意味着要准备适应当地习俗和规范，而不是期望当地环境适应旅行者。

paragraphs.text: Second, tourism is a market-based activity and works best when consumers reward better performers. In the information age, there's little excuse for travelers being uninformed about where their vacation money goes and who it enriches.
paragraphs.translation: 其次，旅游是一种基于市场的活动，当消费者奖励表现更好者时效果最佳。在信息时代，旅行者没有借口不知道他们的度假资金去向和谁因此受益。

paragraphs.text: Informed travelers also are better able to distinguish between multinational companies and local entrepreneurs whose businesses provide direct social, environmental, and economic benefits for local residents. Such businesses are in love with the destination and are therefore deserving of market reward. In the long run, being a responsible traveler means ensuring net positive impacts for local people and environments. With the information available at our fingertips, there has never been more opportunity to do so.
paragraphs.translation: 有见识的旅行者也更能区分跨国公司和当地企业家，后者的业务为当地居民提供直接的社会、环境和经济效益。这些企业热爱目的地，因此值得市场奖励。长远来看，成为负责任的旅行者意味着确保对当地人民和环境产生净积极影响。在信息触手可及的今天，这样做从未有如此多的机会。

You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.questionText: What is the popular assumption about international tourism?

options.label: A
options.text: Its benefits may compensate for the adverse environmental consequences.

options.label: B
options.text: Its rapid development is attributed to people's improved living standard.

options.label: C
options.text: It appeals to people in places with favorable geographical conditions.

options.label: D
options.text: It contributes to the economy of destination countries and regions.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。根据文章第一段'Travel is often portrayed as a tool for personal growth and tourism as an economic motor for destination countries and cities'可知，国际旅游被普遍认为能够促进目的地国家和地区的经济发展。

wrongOptions.A: 文章没有提到国际旅游的益处能补偿对环境的不利影响
wrongOptions.B: 文章没有提到国际旅游的快速发展归因于人们生活水平的提高
wrongOptions.C: 文章没有提到国际旅游吸引地理条件优越地区的人们

questions.questionText: What do we learn from some studies about uncontrolled tourism development?

options.label: A
options.text: It gives rise to an increase in mass confrontations.

options.label: B
options.text: It incurs local residents' antagonism to tourists.

options.label: C
options.text: It inhibits the steady growth of local economy.

options.label: D
options.text: It brings in a large chunk of mobile population.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。根据文章第三段'Uncontrolled tourism development has become a primary driver of social and environmental disruption. Tourism studies provide much documentation of the many negative social impacts of tourism and resulting resentment that local populations direct toward visitors'可知，无序的旅游发展引起了当地居民对游客的敌意。

wrongOptions.A: 文章没有提到无序旅游发展导致大规模对抗的增加
wrongOptions.C: 文章没有提到无序旅游发展抑制了当地经济的稳定增长
wrongOptions.D: 文章没有提到无序旅游发展带来了大量流动人口

questions.questionText: Why does the author say local residents of popular destinations often feel frustrated?

options.label: A
options.text: They fall victim to social conflicts and environmental disturbances.

options.label: B
options.text: They have little opportunity to enjoy themselves on cruise ships.

options.label: C
options.text: They cannot find employment in multinational hotel chains.

options.label: D
options.text: They do not think they benefit as much as they deserve.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。根据文章第四段'Residents often become frustrated when the benefits of tourism are not felt locally'可知，当地居民感到沮丧是因为他们没有感受到旅游带来的好处。

wrongOptions.A: 文章没有提到当地居民成为社会冲突和环境干扰的受害者
wrongOptions.B: 文章没有提到当地居民没有机会在游轮上享受自己
wrongOptions.C: 文章没有提到当地居民不能在跨国酒店连锁中找到工作

questions.questionText: How does the author say local residents in destination communities respond to tourism activity?

options.label: A
options.text: They endeavor to adapt to it.

options.label: B
options.text: They readily adopt new lifestyles.

options.label: C
options.text: They immerse tourists in their culture.

options.label: D
options.text: They try to upgrade their business models.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。题干问目的地社区当地居民对旅游活动如何回应。原文 'data show that tourism activity corresponds to increased social problems as local residents adopt the behaviors of tourists' 是关键句，'adopt the behaviors of tourists'（采纳游客的行为方式）对应上文 'lifestyle transformations'，直接对应 B 选项 'They readily adopt new lifestyles（欣然接受新的生活方式）'。语法上 as 引导的状语从句说明居民主动采纳游客行为，故选 B。

questionGroups.sourceText: 自古以来，印章在中国就是身份的凭证和权力的象征。印章不仅具有实用性，而且也是一种艺术形式，是一门集书法与雕刻于一体的古老艺术，经常被看作与书画并列的独立艺术品。印章从材料的选择、制作的工艺到字体的设计，都具有极其丰富的美学表现。其他国家的艺术家通常在其绘画作品上签名，而中国艺术家则往往在其书画作品上盖上印章代替签名。这样，印章也就成为作品的组成部分，是体现作品独特性的一种方式。

answer.modelTranslation: Since ancient times, the seal has served in China as proof of identity and a symbol of power. A seal is not merely a practical tool but also a form of art — an ancient craft that combines calligraphy and carving, and is often regarded as an independent art form on a par with painting and calligraphy. From the choice of material and the techniques of production to the design of the script, seals exhibit extremely rich aesthetic expression. While artists in other countries usually sign their names on their paintings, Chinese artists tend to stamp a seal on their paintings and calligraphic works in place of a signature. In this way, the seal becomes part of the work itself and a means of conveying its uniqueness.
translationNotes: '自古以来'译为 Since ancient times, 置于句首作时间状语
'身份的凭证和权力的象征' 译为 proof of identity and a symbol of power, 用 and 并列两个名词短语
'集书法与雕刻于一体' 用 combines calligraphy and carving 体现 '集...于一体'
'与书画并列的独立艺术品' 用 on a par with 表示 '与...并列', 比 equal to 更书面
'从材料...到字体' 用 From... to... 结构, 译为 From the choice of material... to the design of the script
'盖上印章代替签名' 处理为 stamp a seal... in place of a signature, 避免直译 'replace'
末句 '体现作品独特性的一种方式' 译为 a means of conveying its uniqueness, 用 means 强调途径
scoringPoints: 准确传达 '印章' 作为身份凭证与权力象征的双重含义
正确处理 '集...于一体' 与 '与...并列' 等中文特有结构
From... to... 并列结构清晰呈现材料、工艺、字体三方面
对比 '其他国家艺术家' 与 '中国艺术家' 的两种签名方式时, 时态、并列得当
末句逻辑衔接自然, 体现 '作品组成部分' 与 '独特性' 的因果
